abandoned_internal_history.reason: Selector hypothesis falsified; Wulver DEV support gate NO_GO; oracle acquisition not allowed.
MECHANISM_COMPOSITE_STATIC_NO_GO; best rule improved WFS 3.11% only and failed mechanism quadrant ordering.
ANALYTIC_INDEX_NO_GO; forms collapsed or inverted quadrant semantics.
Held-out/OOD envelope gain 0.0; selection sufficient for that pair, but native prefill/decode mechanism remains useful evidence.

abandoned_internal_history.idea: KV reserve/LLF switching or hysteresis child
abandoned_internal_history.reason: KV composition safety refinement failed to establish safe envelope expansion; native KV/debt policy can still be distinct if not parent switching.

abandoned_internal_history.idea: Family-A stateful controller as ESTF/WFS mode selector
abandoned_internal_history.reason: STATEFUL_CONTROLLER_NO_GO; it was a selector over parents, not native debt scheduling.
Prior chunk children did not add envelope as two-parent children, but slow-timescale chunk budget coordinated with debt/KV is not yet tested as a native portfolio policy.
WFS uses instantaneous deficit; no native accumulated multi-debt scheduler has been evaluated across the six-policy envelope.

abandoned_internal_history.idea: Two-timescale controller with slow budgets and fast request ranking
abandoned_internal_history.reason: Decision-criticality and public/controlled contrasts suggest memoryless per-decision policies are narrow; no native two-timescale portfolio policy has been screened.

candidate_policy_families.expected_advantage: Targets fairness/SLO, completion pressure, queue-age starvation, KV load, and mixed transitions in one native rule without selecting parents.
candidate_policy_families.expected_failure_mode: May behave like WFS if debt update is too instantaneous, or over-serve debt-heavy classes and lose completion efficiency.
candidate_policy_families.mechanism: Maintain explicit per-class and system debts for service share, waiting age, SLO risk, completion backlog, and KV occupancy; schedule the request with highest normalized debt reduction per predicted service under feasibility guards.
candidate_policy_families.name: PORTFOLIO_SYNTHESIS_DEBT_SCHEDULER
candidate_policy_families.priority_decision_rule: score(req)=debt_pressure(class,system,req)/predicted_service(req) + completion_release_bonus(req) - kv_pressure_penalty(req), with hard feasibility and starvation guards; debts update once per simulator step.
state_inputs: bounded rolling admitted/completed service by class
candidate_policy_families.why_not_redundant: Uses accumulated cross-step debt and direct request ranking, not WFS instantaneous demand/served deficit and not ESTF/WFS parent choice.

candidate_policy_families.expected_advantage: Directly addresses endogenous closed-loop shift and regime persistence.
candidate_policy_families.expected_failure_mode: Budget lag can miss short bursts; too many controls may duplicate previous composition complexity.
candidate_policy_families.mechanism: Slow controller sets service quota, chunk budget, KV reserve, and urgent budget from regime state; fast scheduler ranks requests within those budgets.
candidate_policy_families.name: PORTFOLIO_SYNTHESIS_TWO_TIMESCALE_CONTROLLER
candidate_policy_families.priority_decision_rule: Every M steps update budgets; every step admit/rank by urgency and completion efficiency constrained by slow budgets.
candidate_policy_families.why_not_redundant: Controls chunk/reserve/quota state rather than choosing among fixed policies or blending scores.

candidate_policy_families.expected_advantage: Encodes mechanism evidence without scalar blend and may preserve interpretability.
candidate_policy_families.expected_failure_mode: Hard buckets can be brittle at boundaries and may reproduce LLF/WFS behavior in many states.
candidate_policy_families.mechanism: Hard priority order: deadline-infeasible/near-deadline requests, then debt/starvation guard, then completion-efficient release, then KV-safe placement.
candidate_policy_families.name: PORTFOLIO_SYNTHESIS_LEXICOGRAPHIC_NATIVE_POLICY
candidate_policy_families.priority_decision_rule: Partition requests into protected buckets, then sort lexicographically within the first nonempty bucket.
candidate_policy_families.why_not_redundant: Action space is requests directly; however it is closer to existing LLF/WFS than the debt scheduler.

candidate_policy_families.expected_advantage: Targets KV reserve over-conservatism and completion release simultaneously.
candidate_policy_families.expected_failure_mode: Could duplicate kv_constrained_online except for small completion pockets; may ignore fairness debt.
candidate_policy_families.mechanism: KV reserve plus completion packing: reserve memory for urgent/near-deadline work while prioritizing near-complete or small-KV jobs that release capacity soon.
candidate_policy_families.name: PORTFOLIO_SYNTHESIS_KV_COMPLETION_POLICY
candidate_policy_families.priority_decision_rule: Under high KV pressure, admit requests maximizing expected KV release/completion per token while preserving urgent reserve.
candidate_policy_families.why_not_redundant: Adds completion-release objective to KV reserve, but narrower than debt scheduler.

candidate_policy_families.expected_advantage: Targets public/controlled gap and prefill/decode transient contention.
candidate_policy_families.expected_failure_mode: May add no ANWG if capacity remains saturated/degenerate or reproduce chunked_prefill_small.
candidate_policy_families.mechanism: Stateful burst detector modulates prefill chunk/admission budget and class service credits during arrivals.
candidate_policy_families.name: PORTFOLIO_SYNTHESIS_BURST_AWARE_PREFILL_SHAPER
candidate_policy_families.priority_decision_rule: When burst debt rises, shrink prompt chunks and protect late/urgent classes; relax after debt decays.
candidate_policy_families.why_not_redundant: Stateful burst response rather than static small/full chunking.

mechanistic_novelty_filter.kept_because: All retained families rank/admit requests natively and introduce either accumulated debt, slow-timescale budgets, or direct KV/prefill control.

native_lexicographic_assessment: Viable backup family: more faithful than guarded ESTF/WFS because it chooses requests directly, but higher risk of collapsing to LLF/WFS bucket logic.
stateful_debt_credit_assessment: Most promising next direction. WFS already has instantaneous deficit, but accumulated service/age/SLO/KV debt is distinct and can address long-run fairness/completion tradeoffs that static selectors missed.
two_timescale_assessment: Scientifically promising: decision-criticality and closed-loop failures suggest memoryless per-decision selection is too narrow. However, starting with a debt scheduler is cleaner because it can be implemented as one native policy while still leaving room for bounded debt updates.
